latency.scope: RPC uses the historical submit-to-checked-epilogue interval. Caller deadlines and native expiry replies are matched by exact request pointer and client DP. VBI rounding is excluded from deadline latency.

limits.scope: Compare matched optimized configurations and workloads: 10 gestures per widget cohort and 30 pointer motions/button edges. Development measurements, not qualification.
limits.explanation: 20.1 ms allows one PAL scanout-observation frame of phase difference. CPU/consumption budgets are explicit integration allowances, not measured jitter. No deliberate extra-frame wait is allowed. Exceedances require investigation before AS4 acceptance.

comparison.scope: Loaded allowance applies when either GEM clients or native scroll/disk work is active. Both frozen AS0 and matched AES-disabled comparisons are retained. Combined visibility includes the sequential label-observation upper bound.

optimization.change: Use successful alarm completion as expiry proof. Requery the clock only when a message precedes terminal alarm publication; preserve error-before-consume and simultaneous readiness.

rpc.scope: Registration and orderly exit around the same idle observation; GUI lock latency is not sampled here.

optimization.workload: Original continuously exchanging GEM loops and 100 ms delay retained. Counts are completions in bounded windows, not equal offered throughput or a saturated throughput benchmark. The faster implementation completes more work; no fixed-rate cohort replaces the original acceptance workloads.

upper_ram.reservations: Global arena, C banks, native code banks and stack/DP pools unchanged from the prior integrated proof.

demo.scope: Desktop OF816 autoboot, widget toggle/radio/momentary/cancel/disabled/default, client drag/focus, disk commands, writable WORK media, seven-Task pipeline and EXIT
demo.note: Production native desktop preview, separate from the optional two-GEM-client proof. Includes OF816, matching SYS/WORK disks, pinned ROM, guide, upstream licenses and SHA256SUMS. The optimized AES C helper is not linked into this native-only preview. Standard shell/prime build defaults are unchanged.

scope: Focused development tests; no release or physical-hardware qualification.
Four-client capacity/ownership and raw/optimized bridge checks are retained from HY1-HY3; final changed matching helper rerun on PAL/NTSC.
Final integrated image replayed with and without observation; update/mouse locks, deferred gestures, CPU peer, disk/scroll progress, repeated attach/exit/restart and clean shutdown.
57.6k SIO envelope only; existing 125k limitation remains separate.
Disabled comparisons reuse checksum-verified frozen native artifacts. Idle registered controls remain at HY3: the changed helper is never called by parked clients in that cohort.
Boundary and zero-wake checks used the pre-optimization image with identical adapter, interrupt, scheduler and presenter code. Final pointer/call cohorts also validate physical capture and ownership.
conclusion: The hybrid transport is functional and eliminates migrated-call presenter dispatch, but active GUI latency still exceeds the unchanged original limits and several existing follow-up measurements. Idle registration passes the original AS0 limits, while the additional frozen-disabled comparison has small scroll overruns. HY4 and the AS4/TD4 successor performance gate remain unaccepted. Caller CPU reductions alone do not close the gate; further CPU/scheduling/presenter latency work needs separate scope. Priorities and physical drawing ownership remain unchanged.
